reason: Reproduced through transformItems: Poco no me sirvió, la verdad (u60-t-0039), Contá cómo no te fue con el abogado, and ¿Raras veces no cocinas tú en casa?, which the u60 render serves as a live card, while the node's own pitfall strikes out Poco no importa ya. The fix is in code: POLARITY in spanish.ts lists mucho but not poco or raras, negate must refuse a verb inside an embedded cómo clause, and the same row also yields Poco me la sirvió,. from pronominalise.

A simplification rather than an error, and 'taught nowhere' overstates it (g:topic-fronting says new information lands at the end, g:parecer-quedar puts the thing after the verb). Presentational verbs do favour the subject after the verb (faltan agujas, Meyer-Hermann via Borzi), but nearly all verbs allow both orders, so 'usually' becomes 'often, when it is the news', and I keep the words Normal order because the last paragraph refers back to them.
quote: Normal order puts the subject first: *El barrio ha cambiado mucho.*
replacement: Normal order puts the subject first with most verbs: *El barrio ha cambiado mucho.* With *llegar*, *quedar* and *faltar* it often comes after, when it is the news: *llegó Vale*.

reason: Focus fronting is a marked assertive device needing emphatic intonation (Leonetti and Escandell Vidal, via an abstract), and here it answers a neutral English question whose natural Spanish, ¿Has cambiado mucho en estos años?, is rejected (tested). Deleting a row is not a string swap: the row floor of 12 and the 4 question minimum still hold (5 dialogue rows pass isQuestionRow), but the node drops under the 40 row drill target, so top up with dialogue rows like 0018 to 0021.
quote: ¿Mucho has cambiado tú en estos años?

reason: The claim's ground fails: this is an alternative question, not a yes or no question, and those license a fronted choice in ordinary speech (¿Frío o caliente lo quieres?, from memory), so the row is acceptable, unlike its neighbours. Its one weakness is that ¿Has aprendido poco o mucho este año? would be rejected, which an accept entry would solve.
quote: ¿Poco o mucho has aprendido este año?

reason: A fronted predicate adjective with *es* right after it belongs to assertive written Spanish; as a neutral question to a friend it is plainly unnatural, where anyone says ¿Es difícil para ti decir que no? or ¿Te cuesta decir que no? The fix is a row deletion, see LC1-073 for the supply effect.
quote: ¿Difícil es para ti decir que no?

reason: The syntax holds and the claim misclassifies it: frequency adverbs sit before the verb with no focus effect, as in ¿Nunca cocinas en casa?, so this is not literary fronting. Whether a Colombian would ever ask it with bookish raras veces rather than casi nunca is a usage call I cannot settle; the generated negation of this row is LC1-002's bug either way.
quote: ¿Raras veces cocinas tú en casa?

reason: Rows u59-1041 (para vos) and u59-1138 (te enredás) rely on forms the rule never mentions. Vos after prepositions with te as the object is standard voseo (DPD voseo entry from memory, and a learner source I searched says the same), and the addition fits with the commands sentence it extends.

replacement: Commands also put the stress at the end: *vení* (*ven*), *sentate* (*siéntate*). After a preposition it stays *vos* (*para vos*, *con vos*), and the object word stays *te*: *¿vos te acordás?*

reason: Both rejections reproduced, and NGLE Manual 24.1.2g (via UDEP's Castellano Actual; I could not open the DPD) backs habría and hubiera alternating, with a stronger preference for hubiera in America. But 'any imperfect subjunctive' overreaches: where -ra stands for the conditional (quisiera, pudiera, debiera) -se is anomalous, so the code must scope the -ra and -se swap to subordinate clauses and the hubiera swap to result clauses, never the si clause.

The script's own examples (Es caro; o sea, no lo podemos pagar and Tomás no quiere vender; en otras palabras, el café sigue abierto) add a consequence, so 'never a new fact' is false. Whether conclusion is a value of o sea or a relation it introduces is debated (Murillo), and the replacement holds either way; I could not open the DPDE entry.
quote: What follows is never a new fact. It is the first fact, made clearer.
replacement: What follows is the first idea made clearer, or what it comes down to.

reason: 'No que, no conclusion' is false: g:reformulation has Es caro; o sea, no lo podemos pagar, and u14-0296 has El loro dijo mi nombre, o sea, me conoce. I drop 'with no comma' because u14-0216 and u14-0217 write O sea, que no vienes, and the fix does not need that absolute.

replacement: Note the *que*: *o sea que* runs straight into the sentence. *O sea* on its own takes a comma: *o sea, Tomás se queda*.

replacement: Almost. Join it with *que*, or put a comma after *o sea*.

replacement: With *lo que*, ask yourself: pointed at, or still open? With *el hecho de que*, the question is different: are you reacting to it? Then the subjunctive.
